_about: Field terms for F166, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

cpt.definition: a model of choice between gambles with a value function concave for gains and steeper for losses, a loss aversion coefficient and a probability weighting function applied to cumulative probabilities; here six parameters
cpt.excludes: any account of the feelings or brain processes behind a choice

loss-aversion.definition: the factor lambda by which a loss weighs more than an equal gain in the value function; 1 means losses and gains count alike
loss-aversion.excludes: a dislike of risk as such, which curvature and weighting carry

probability-weighting.definition: a function that maps a stated probability to the weight a choice gives it, so that small chances can count for more than their size and large ones for less
probability-weighting.excludes: a person's belief about the odds, which in these problems are stated

meta-analysis.definition: the statistical pooling of published estimates of one quantity into a summary and a measure of their spread

description-experience-gap.definition: the pattern that people choose as if they overweight rare events when choosing from stated odds and underweight them when they learn the odds from sampled outcomes

combined-formula.definition: CPT's value difference plus four added terms in one choice rule: entropy for information, loss probability for threat, and the mean and mean square of outcomes for drive toward a setpoint; ten parameters
combined-formula.excludes: any claim about mechanisms in the brain, and any reading of the terms other than this operationalisation

description-setting.definition: the 1,928 choices13k problems answered without outcome feedback, where people chose from stated odds alone
description-setting.excludes: the 9,831 problems answered with feedback on outcomes

log-odds.definition: for a rate p, the natural log of p divided by 1 minus p; 0 at an even split and unbounded toward certainty
log-odds.excludes: any information beyond the rate, of which it is a rescaling

binomial-likelihood.definition: fitting by choosing the parameters under which the observed counts of B choices are most probable, treating each choice as an independent draw at the predicted rate; here five choices per listed participant
binomial-likelihood.excludes: extra scatter between problems, which the dispersion handles

expected-value.definition: the probability-weighted average payoff of a gamble, used here as the baseline value model
expected-value.excludes: any allowance for risk, loss or probability weighting

rank-dependent.definition: decision weights that depend on where an outcome ranks among a gamble's outcomes, taken as differences of the weighting function at cumulative probabilities
rank-dependent.excludes: weighting each outcome's probability on its own, as the original 1979 prospect theory did

prelec.definition: a two-parameter probability weighting function, exp of minus delta times minus log p to the power gamma, that sets the curvature and the crossing point of the curve separately
prelec.excludes: the one-parameter Tversky and Kahneman function used in CPT

shannon-entropy.definition: minus the sum of p log2 p over a gamble's outcomes, in bits: how uncertain the outcome is before it happens, 0 for a sure thing

drive-reduction.definition: for a setpoint S, the quantity S squared minus (S minus x) squared for an outcome x, whose expectation is linear in the mean and mean square of outcomes
drive-reduction.excludes: any measured need or state of the people choosing

cv-r2.definition: one minus the squared error of out-of-fold predictions over the variance of the observed rates, with 10 folds grouped by problem: the share of variance that predictions made without seeing those rates account for
cv-r2.excludes: in-sample R², which rewards fitting noise

bic.definition: the Bayesian information criterion with the log-likelihood divided by the dispersion: a score that trades fit against the number of parameters, lower being better
bic.excludes: an absolute test of a model, since it only compares models on the same data

dispersion.definition: the factor phi by which observed rates scatter more than independent binomial choices would allow, taken from the COMB fit in each setting

boosted-trees.definition: a predictor built by adding many small decision trees, each fitted to what the previous ones missed; here a flexible learner's score on the same folds
boosted-trees.excludes: a theory of choice, since it states no value function

sampling-ceiling.definition: one minus the mean sampling variance of the observed rates over their variance across problems: the share of variance not explained by finite samples of participants
sampling-ceiling.excludes: noise of other kinds, such as the structured decision noise reported for these data

offset.definition: a part of the prediction fixed in advance and never refitted; here the fitted CPT log odds, so an added term can only explain what CPT leaves over
offset.excludes: refitting CPT together with the added term

irls.definition: the standard routine for fitting a logistic model by repeated weighted least-squares steps
irls.excludes: any effect on what is tested, since it is only the fitting method

deviance.definition: twice the log-likelihood shortfall of a model against a perfect fit; a deviance gain is the fall in deviance when a term is added
deviance.excludes: any penalty for the added parameter

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values into q values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

bootstrap.definition: refitting a model many times on problems resampled with replacement to read how much an estimate varies
bootstrap.excludes: an interval from a textbook formula that assumes a distribution

extra-binomial.definition: scatter in a choice rate from problem to problem beyond what independent choices would give, simulated here with a Beta distribution

false-success.definition: a run of the full procedure on data simulated with no added effect, showing how large a gain the procedure finds when there is nothing to find
false-success.excludes: a planted check, which asks whether a real effect is found
